country.name: Albania
country.tagline: Kallmet, Shesh and Pulës: native grapes on the Adriatic hills, recovering from a century of upheaval.

stats.note: Wikipedia (national statistics): 10,178 ha of vineyard and 204,000 t of grapes in 2015; no reliable recent wine-production figure found.

country.overview:
Albania has grown vines since the Illyrians, at least 3,000 years ago, and the Greek and Roman colonies of the coast (Apollonia, Dyrrhachium, Butrint) left wine imagery in their ruins. The Ottoman centuries reduced vineyards largely to Christian areas, phylloxera nearly destroyed what remained by 1933, and after 1945 the Communist regime planted collective vineyards (from about 2,700 ha after the war to over 17,000 ha by 1990) for brandy and bulk wine. The collapse of 1991 and the privatisation chaos that followed broke up those estates; today about 10,000 ha are planted, mostly for table grapes and home wine and raki, and a few dozen commercial wineries are building a modern identity.

That identity rests on native grapes. Kallmet, a red named after the village of Kallmet near Lezhë, grows on the Zadrima plain between Shkodër and Lezhë and makes dark, spicy wines. Shesh i Zi (black) and Shesh i Bardhë (white) take their name from Shesh, near Tirana, and are the most widespread. Pulës is a white of Berat, Debinë a white from the south-east (Korçë, Përmet), and Vlosh a red of the Vlorë coast. The best-known producers include Kantina Arbëri in Mirditë (Kallmet), Çobo near Berat (Pulës and Shesh), Kokomani near Tirana, Nurellari in Skrapar, Skënderbeu and Bardha.

Albania is an EU candidate. Under its trade agreement with the United Kingdom, 36 Albanian wine names, essentially its historic districts from Shkodër and Koplik to Korçë, Përmet, Berat and Sarandë, are protected as geographical indications.

history.title: Illyrian and Greek vines
history.text: Illyrian tribes and the Greek colonies of Epidamnos (Durrës) and Apollonia grew and traded wine; Roman Butrint's decorations show its importance.

history.title: Phylloxera
history.text: Phylloxera nearly wiped out Albanian viticulture; after the Second World War only about 2,737 ha remained.

history.title: Collective vineyards
history.text: The Communist state expanded vineyards to about 17,600 ha by 1990 for wine and brandy, but exports fell from 61,000 hl (1971) to 22,000 hl (1985).

history.title: Private revival
history.text: After 1991 collective farms were dismantled and family wineries emerged, focusing on Kallmet, Shesh, Pulës and Debinë.

country.classification: Albania is not in the EU and has no EU-registered wine PDOs or PGIs. Under the UK-Albania trade agreement, 36 Albanian wine names are protected in the UK as geographical indications, corresponding to the country's historic districts (rrethe): Berat, Bulqizë, Delvinë, Devoll, Dibër, Durrës, Elbasan, Fier, Gjirokastër, Gramsh, Has, Kavajë, Kolonjë, Koplik, Korçë, Krujë, Kukës, Kurbin, Kuçovë, Lezhë, Librazhd, Lushnjë, Mallakastër, Mat, Mirditë, Peqin, Pogradec, Pukë, Përmet, Sarandë, Shkodër, Skrapar, Tepelenë, Tiranë, Tropojë and Vlorë.
country.climate_soils: The coastal plain and hills are Mediterranean, with hot dry summers; the interior and the south-eastern highlands around Korçë are continental and cooler. Soils range from alluvial plains to limestone and flysch hills.

grapes.name: Kallmet
grapes.note: Native red of the Zadrima plain near Lezhë and Shkodër, named after the village of Kallmet.

grapes.name: Shesh i Zi and Shesh i Bardhë
grapes.note: Red and white grapes named after Shesh near Tirana; the most widespread natives.

regions.name: Northern Albania
regions.tagline: The Zadrima plain and the hills of Shkodër, Lezhë and Mirditë: Kallmet country.
regions.summary: The north (Shkodër, Koplik, Lezhë, Kurbin, Mirditë, Pukë) is the home of Kallmet, grown on the alluvial Zadrima plain and surrounding hills where the Drin reaches the sea. Kantina Arbëri in Mirditë and family wineries around Shkodër and Lezhë lead.
regions.history: The Catholic north kept vineyards through the Ottoman period.
regions.terroir: Alluvial plains and limestone hills; Mediterranean with high rainfall.
regions.grapes: Kallmet, Shesh i Zi, Shesh i Bardhë.
regions.classification: UK-protected GIs Shkodër, Koplik, Lezhë, Kurbin, Mirditë, Pukë and others.

sources.title: GOV.UK protected food and drink names register (Albanian wine GIs)

regions.name: Central and Southern Albania
regions.tagline: Tirana's Shesh, Berat's Pulës and the Debinë of Korçë and Përmet.
regions.summary: Central and southern Albania include Tirana (Shesh), Durrës and Kavajë on the coast, Berat (Pulës, Çobo winery), Skrapar (Nurellari), Vlorë (Vlosh), and the highlands of Korçë and Përmet (Debinë).
regions.history: Greek and Roman Apollonia, Butrint and Berat give the region a deep wine history.
regions.terroir: Coastal hills, river valleys and continental highlands.
regions.grapes: Shesh i Zi, Shesh i Bardhë, Pulës, Debinë, Vlosh, Serinë, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon.
regions.classification: UK-protected GIs Tiranë, Berat, Korçë, Përmet, Vlorë, Skrapar and others.

al-berat.name: Berat

sites.name: Kallmet
sites.text: The village of Kallmet near Lezhë gave its name to Albania's most famous native red grape, grown on the surrounding Zadrima plain and hills. The village is part of the Catholic north, where vineyards survived the Ottoman centuries.

sites.name: Çobo winery
sites.text: The Çobo family winery at Ura Vajgurore near Berat is one of Albania's best-known estates, championing the local white Pulës and the red Shesh i Zi.

sites.name: Kokomani winery
sites.text: Kantina Kokomani at Ndroq, west of Tirana, is a modern family winery making Shesh and international varieties from the coastal hills between the capital and Durrës.

sites.name: Nurellari winery
sites.text: Nurellari's winery near Poliçan in the Osum valley of Skrapar, south-east of Berat, makes wines from local and international grapes in Albania's rugged southern interior.
